exercise.instruction: Make sentences from the words in brackets. Put the verb into the correct form: present perfect (I have done), present perfect continuous (I have been doing), past perfect (I had done) or past perfect continuous (I had been doing).

parts: We were all surprised when Jess and Nick got married last year.
answers: They’d only known each other (for) a few weeks
They had only known each other (for) a few weeks

parts: It’s still raining. I wish it would stop.
answers: It has been raining all day

parts: Suddenly I woke up. I was confused and didn’t know where I was.
It was lunchtime, but I wasn’t hungry. I didn’t want to eat anything.
answers: I had had a big breakfast

parts: Every year Robert and Tina spend a few days at the same hotel by the sea.
answers: They’ve been going there for years
They have been going there for years
I’ve had it since I got up
I have had it since I got up

parts: Next month Gary is going to run in a marathon.
answers: He’s been training very hard for it
He has been training very hard for it
